passages.text: In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: We have a strong city; salvation is established as its walls and ramparts.
passages.sermon:
On that day, people in Judah will sing a song.
The people will say, “We have a strong city.”
God makes salvation its walls.
God makes salvation its ramparts.
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יוּשַׁ֥ר הַשִּׁיר־ הַזֶּ֖ה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֑ה עִ֣יר עָז־ לָ֔נוּ יְשׁוּעָ֥ה יָשִׁ֖ית חוֹמ֥וֹת וָחֵֽל׃

passages.text: Open the gates so a righteous nation may enter— one that remains faithful.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
He commands them to open the gates.
He wants a righteous nation to enter.
This nation does what is right.
This nation remains faithful to God.
passages.original: פִּתְח֖וּ שְׁעָרִ֑ים וְיָבֹ֥א גוֹי־ צַדִּ֖יק שֹׁמֵ֥ר אֱמֻנִֽים׃

passages.text: You will keep in perfect peace the steadfast of mind, because he trusts in You.
passages.sermon:
God keeps people in perfect peace.
These people have steadfast minds.
They trust in God.
God gives them peace because they trust Him.
passages.original: יֵ֣צֶר סָמ֔וּךְ תִּצֹּ֖ר שָׁל֣וֹם׀ שָׁל֑וֹם כִּ֥י בְךָ֖ בָּטֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: Trust in the LORD forever, because GOD the LORD is the Rock eternal.
passages.sermon:
Trust in the LORD.
Trust Him forever.
The LORD is God.
The LORD is the Rock.
He is the eternal Rock.
passages.original: בִּטְח֥וּ בַֽיהוָ֖ה עֲדֵי־ עַ֑ד כִּ֚י בְּיָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה צ֖וּר עוֹלָמִֽים׃

passages.text: For He has humbled those who dwell on high; He lays the lofty city low. He brings it down to the ground; He casts it into the dust.
passages.sermon:
God acts with power.
God humbles people who live in high places.
God brings down those who are proud.
God makes the lofty city fall.
God brings the city down to the ground.
God throws it into the dust.
passages.original: כִּ֤י הֵשַׁח֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י מָר֔וֹם קִרְיָ֖ה נִשְׂגָּבָ֑ה יַשְׁפִּילֶ֤נָּה יַשְׁפִּילָהּ֙ עַד־ אֶ֔רֶץ יַגִּיעֶ֖נָּה עַד־ עָפָֽר׃

passages.text: Feet trample it down— the feet of the oppressed, the steps of the poor.
passages.sermon: The feet of the oppressed trample the city down.\r\nThe steps of the poor crush it underfoot.
passages.original: תִּרְמְסֶ֖נָּה רָ֑גֶל רַגְלֵ֥י עָנִ֖י פַּעֲמֵ֥י דַלִּֽים׃

passages.text: The path of the righteous is level; You clear a straight path for the upright.
passages.sermon: God makes the way clear for righteous people.\r\nGod makes the path level for those who do what is right.\r\nGod prepares a straight road for upright people.
passages.original: אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים יָשָׁ֕ר מַעְגַּ֥ל צַדִּ֖יק תְּפַלֵּֽס׃

passages.text: Yes, we wait for You, O LORD; we walk in the path of Your judgments. Your name and renown are the desire of our souls.
passages.sermon:
We wait for you, LORD.
We walk in the path of your judgments.
Your name is the desire of our souls.
Your fame is the desire of our souls.
passages.original: אַ֣ף אֹ֧רַח מִשְׁפָּטֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה קִוִּינ֑וּךָ לְשִׁמְךָ֥ וּֽלְזִכְרְךָ֖ תַּאֲוַת־ נָֽפֶשׁ׃

passages.text: My soul longs for You in the night; indeed, my spirit seeks You at dawn. For when Your judgments come upon the earth, the people of the world learn righteousness.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a person who seeks God.
This person desires God deeply.
At night, my soul longs for You, God.
In the morning, my spirit seeks You, God.
When You, God, bring Your judgments to the earth, people learn what is right.
The people of the world learn righteousness when You judge the earth.
passages.original: נַפְשִׁ֤י אִוִּיתִ֙יךָ֙ בַּלַּ֔יְלָה אַף־ רוּחִ֥י בְקִרְבִּ֖י אֲשַֽׁחֲרֶ֑ךָּ כִּ֞י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר מִשְׁפָּטֶ֙יךָ֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ צֶ֥דֶק לָמְד֖וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃

passages.text: Though grace is shown to the wicked man, he does not learn righteousness. In the land of righteousness he acts unjustly and fails to see the majesty of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The wicked man receives grace.
He does not learn righteousness.
He lives in a land of righteousness.
He acts unjustly there.
He does not see the majesty of the LORD.
passages.original: יֻחַ֤ן רָשָׁע֙ בַּל־ לָמַ֣ד צֶ֔דֶק בְּאֶ֥רֶץ נְכֹח֖וֹת יְעַוֵּ֑ל וּבַל־ יִרְאֶ֖ה גֵּא֥וּת יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: O LORD, Your hand is upraised, but they do not see it. They will see Your zeal for Your people and be put to shame. The fire set for Your enemies will consume them!
passages.sermon:
The LORD is powerful.
The LORD lifts up His hand.
The wicked do not see His power.
They will see the LORD’s zeal for His people.
They will feel shame.
The fire prepared for the LORD’s enemies will consume them.
passages.original: יְהוָ֛ה רָ֥מָה יָדְךָ֖ בַּל־ יֶחֱזָי֑וּן יֶחֱז֤וּ וְיֵבֹ֙שׁוּ֙ קִנְאַת־ עָ֔ם אַף־ אֵ֖שׁ צָרֶ֥יךָ תֹאכְלֵֽם׃ס

passages.text: O LORD, You will establish peace for us. For all that we have accomplished, You have done for us.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our God.
The LORD will give us peace.
The LORD will make peace for us.
The LORD has done everything we have accomplished.
All our works come from the LORD.
passages.original: יְהוָ֕ה תִּשְׁפֹּ֥ת שָׁל֖וֹם לָ֑נוּ כִּ֛י גַּ֥ם כָּֽל־ מַעֲשֵׂ֖ינוּ פָּעַ֥לְתָּ לָּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: O LORD our God, other lords besides You have had dominion, but Your name alone do we confess.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our God.
Other masters have ruled over us.
These masters are not You.
We confess only Your name.
We remember only You.
passages.original: יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ בְּעָל֥וּנוּ אֲדֹנִ֖ים זֽוּלָתֶ֑ךָ לְבַד־ בְּךָ֖ נַזְכִּ֥יר שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: The dead will not live; the departed spirits will not rise. Therefore You have punished and destroyed them; You have wiped out all memory of them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the subject.
The LORD has power over life and death.
The dead will not live.
The departed spirits will not rise.
The LORD has punished them.
The LORD has destroyed them.
The LORD has wiped out all memory of them.
passages.original: מֵתִים֙ בַּל־ יִחְי֔וּ רְפָאִ֖ים בַּל־ יָקֻ֑מוּ לָכֵ֤ן פָּקַ֙דְתָּ֙ וַתַּשְׁמִידֵ֔ם וַתְּאַבֵּ֥ד כָּל־ זֵ֖כֶר לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: You have enlarged the nation, O LORD; You have enlarged the nation. You have gained glory for Yourself; You have extended all the borders of the land.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our God.
The LORD made the nation larger.
The LORD increased the nation again.
The LORD gained glory for Himself.
The LORD pushed out all the borders of the land.
passages.original: יָסַ֤פְתָּ לַגּוֹי֙ יְהוָ֔ה יָסַ֥פְתָּ לַגּ֖וֹי נִכְבָּ֑דְתָּ רִחַ֖קְתָּ כָּל־ קַצְוֵי־ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: O LORD, they sought You in their distress; when You disciplined them, they poured out a quiet prayer.
passages.sermon:
The people felt distress.
They looked for You, O LORD.
You disciplined them.
They prayed quietly to You.
passages.original: יְהוָ֖ה בַּצַּ֣ר פְּקָד֑וּךָ צָק֣וּן לַ֔חַשׁ מוּסָרְךָ֖ לָֽמוֹ׃

passages.text: As a woman with child about to give birth writhes and cries out in pain, so were we in Your presence, O LORD.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel suffered before the LORD.
They felt pain and distress.
A woman about to give birth feels pain.
She cries out as she labors.
In the same way, the people cried out before the LORD.
passages.original: כְּמ֤וֹ הָרָה֙ תַּקְרִ֣יב לָלֶ֔דֶת תָּחִ֥יל תִּזְעַ֖ק בַּחֲבָלֶ֑יהָ כֵּ֛ן הָיִ֥ינוּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: We were with child; we writhed in pain; but we gave birth to wind. We have given no salvation to the earth, nor brought any life into the world.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel suffered.
They hoped for deliverance.
They felt pain like a woman in labor.
They expected new life.
But they gave birth only to wind.
They did not bring salvation to the earth.
They did not give life to the people of the world.
passages.original: הָרִ֣ינוּ חַ֔לְנוּ כְּמ֖וֹ יָלַ֣דְנוּ ר֑וּחַ יְשׁוּעֹת֙ בַּל־ נַ֣עֲשֶׂה אֶ֔רֶץ וּבַֽל־ יִפְּל֖וּ יֹשְׁבֵ֥י תֵבֵֽל׃

passages.text: Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is like the dew of the morning, and the earth will bring forth her dead.
passages.sermon:
God is speaking to His people.
God promises hope and resurrection.
Your dead will live.
Their bodies will rise.
You who dwell in the dust, awake.
Sing with joy.
God’s dew is like the dew of the morning.
The earth will bring forth her dead.
passages.original: יִֽחְי֣וּ מֵתֶ֔יךָ נְבֵלָתִ֖י יְקוּמ֑וּן הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר כִּ֣י טַ֤ל אוֹרֹת֙ טַלֶּ֔ךָ וָאָ֖רֶץ רְפָאִ֥ים תַּפִּֽיל׃ס

passages.text: Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourselves a little while until the wrath has passed.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
He calls them "my people."
He tells them to go into their rooms.
He commands them to shut their doors behind them.
He tells them to hide for a short time.
He says to wait until His anger passes.
passages.original: לֵ֤ךְ עַמִּי֙ בֹּ֣א בַחֲדָרֶ֔יךָ וּֽסְגֹ֥ר דְּלָתֶיךָ בַּעֲדֶ֑ךָ חֲבִ֥י כִמְעַט־ רֶ֖גַע עַד־ יַעֲבוֹר זָֽעַם׃

passages.text: For behold, the LORD is coming out of His dwelling to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity. The earth will reveal her bloodshed and will no longer conceal her slain.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is holy and just.
The LORD lives in heaven.
The LORD will come out from His dwelling place.
The LORD will punish the people who live on the earth.
He will punish them for their sins.
The earth will show the blood that was shed.
The earth will not hide those who were killed anymore.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִנֵּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יֹצֵ֣א מִמְּקוֹמ֔וֹ לִפְקֹ֛ד עֲוֺ֥ן יֹֽשֵׁב־ הָאָ֖רֶץ עָלָ֑יו וְגִלְּתָ֤ה הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ אֶת־ דָּמֶ֔יהָ וְלֹֽא־ תְכַסֶּ֥ה ע֖וֹד עַל־ הֲרוּגֶֽיהָ׃ס
